description: We are Void Seekers, a passionate multidisciplinary team from Egypt participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are building an interactive 3D web platform for the Offloaded, But Not Forgotten challenge to showcase humanity's historic space hardware on the Moon, Mars, and deep space.
summary:
Project Overview & Concept
Over decades of space exploration, humanity has left remarkable rovers, landers, and probes across the solar system—instruments that completed groundbreaking missions yet remain silent monuments of human ingenuity. Void Seekers bridges NASA’s historical archives with modern web interactivity, enabling users to explore and understand the stories behind discarded space hardware.
How It Works & Key Features
• Three Exploration Zones: Organizes historic hardware across The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space for structured navigation.
• Interactive 3D Visualization: Replaces static photos with manipulable 3D models, allowing users to rotate, zoom, and inspect spacecraft structures.
• Locations & Historical Context: Displays verified mission dates, status, historical impact, and exact coordinates or trajectories.
• Dual-Level Modes: Features a Simple View with engaging, jargon-free storytelling for students, alongside an Advanced View offering deep engineering specs and telemetry for researchers.
Impact
Combining 3D visualization, geospatial tracking, and adaptive storytelling, Void Seekers serves as an accessible educational tool and interactive reference ensuring pioneering space hardware is never forgotten

Project Overview & Concept
Over decades of space exploration, humanity has left remarkable rovers, landers, and probes across the solar system—instruments that completed groundbreaking missions yet remain silent monuments of human ingenuity. Void Seekers bridges NASA’s historical archives with modern web interactivity, enabling users to explore and understand the stories behind discarded space hardware.

How It Works & Key Features
- Three Exploration Zones: Organizes historic hardware across The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space for structured navigation.
- Interactive 3D Visualization: Replaces static photos with manipulable 3D models, allowing users to rotate, zoom, and inspect spacecraft structures.
- Locations & Historical Context: Displays verified mission dates, status, historical impact, and exact coordinates or trajectories.
- Dual-Level Modes: Features a Simple View with engaging, jargon-free storytelling for students, alongside an Advanced View offering deep engineering specs and telemetry for researchers.

Tools, Technologies & Creative Approach
We built Void Seekers using modern web development technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and interactive 3D web libraries) integrated with official NASA archival mission datasets and 3D spacecraft models. Our creative approach focused on transforming static historical records into a spatial, dual-mode learning experience—considering usability for both young students and advanced space enthusiasts.

Impact
Combining 3D visualization, geospatial tracking, and adaptive storytelling, Void Seekers serves as an accessible educational tool and interactive reference ensuring pioneering space hardware is never forgotten.
